# EvAlertDialog

> A blocking dialog that asks the user to confirm or decide - traps focus, closes on Escape, and restores focus on close.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:alert-dialog` |
| Layer | Organism (`src/organisms`) |
| Import | `import { EvAlertDialog } from 'evoq-ui'` |
| Template tag | `<EvAlertDialog>` or `<ev-alert-dialog>` |
| Source | `src/organisms/alert-dialog/EvAlertDialog.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the inner `<div class="ev-alert-dialog__panel">`, not the root |

## Example

```vue
<EvAlertDialog
  title="Hapus dokumen?"
  description="Dokumen tidak bisa dikembalikan."
/>
```

_The exact snippet the playground simulator copies for this component (`playground/simulator-demos.ts`)._

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Alert Dialog**, frame `4147:64224` (Alert Dialog). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use to confirm a consequential or destructive action — delete, discard, sign out — where the user must explicitly decide before proceeding.

### When not to use

- Non-blocking message → use Alert (`evoq-ui:alert`) or Toast. Complex form or multi-step flow → use Modal (`evoq-ui:modal`) / Dialog. Simple inline confirmation → avoid a modal entirely.

### Do

- State the consequence clearly in the title. Use a verb for the primary button (Delete, Continue). Keep the safe choice as Cancel on the left.

### Don't

- Don't use vague labels like OK or Yes. Don't make the destructive action the default focus. Don't stack multiple alert dialogs.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvAlertDialog`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the inner `<div class="ev-alert-dialog__panel">`, not the root.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:alert-dialog` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
